newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
GOLD,SILVER SIEZED IN CHUNKS FROM EX-CHIEF MINISTER'S HOUSES

The recent raids conducted on the houses of J. Jayalalitha, former chief minister of Tamil Nadu (TN), led to the seizure of 30 kg of gold and half a tonne of silver worth around 580 million rupees. The prosecution counsel, opposing granting of bail to the ex-chief minister, stated this in a Madras court. The former TN chief minister is in jail following legal action over her alleged role in the recently unearthed television scam. Jayalalitha was arrested on Saturday for alleged irregularities in the purchase of 45,000 television sets for installation in rural areas, that she had cleared during her tenure as the state chief minister. She denied any wrongdoing.
The Economic Times
LEFT PARTIES WOULD BE TALKED TO ON INSURANCE BILL

The government will take the Left parties into confidence before introducing the proposed Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA). Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda has assured this in a bid to placate the Left which was opposed to liberalisation of the insurance sector. The Left was concerned about clandestine moves being made by the government to open up the Indian insurance sector to foreign and private domestic firms. Judged against this backdrop, the premier's move to take the Left into confidence could have been prompted by the realisation that it would be unwise to ignore the concerns of the Left.
INDIA TO BACK SOME PROPOSALS AT WTO MEET

India is ready to support agreements in three new areas within the World Trade Organisation (WTO). They are liberalisation of information technology, transference in government procurement and trade facilitation. India, however, has decided to oppose any role being played by the WTO in investment, competition policy or labour standards. Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah stated this at the WTO ministerial conference at Singapore.
JINDALS TO DILUTE STAKE IN VIJAYANAGAR STEEL

The promoters of the 25 billion rupee Jindal group may dilute their stake in the 41.38 billion rupee Vijayanagar Steel plant at Bellary, Karnataka. According to sources, the Jindals, who hold 47.7 percent stake in Jindal Vijayanagar Steel Ltd (JVSL) equity, are planning to offload a substantial chunk of their holding to a foreign partner. JVSL is said to be in talks with steel majors like Sumitomo and NKK of Japan, Ilva of Italy and UK's British Steel Company for a technical tie-up. The company has already tied up with 100 expatriates, who now form part of its technical team to run the project at Bellary.
FUJI BANK EYEING CORE SECTOR

Japanese banking major Fuji Bank is turning its eyes towards the Indian infrastructure sector. The bank is closely watching sectors like power and telecommunication. This was stated by the bank's president Yoshiro Yamamoto before a gathering of journalists in Bombay. Yamamoto said the bank, through its Singapore office, had participated in the financing of Dabhol Power Company. Fuji Bank, through its Bombay and Singapore branches, was planning to work in tandem to fund core sector projectors in India, he added. The bank has $500 million worth of exposure in India by way of loans to government-owned corporations and other Indian corporates.
HYUNDAI, ELCOT TO SET UP ELECTRONIC AUTO SPARE UNIT

Hyundai Electronics Company is likely to sign a joint venture pact with Electronics Corporation of Tamil Nadu (Elcot). A team of Hyundai Electronics, the South Korea based electronic automotive component major, is visiting India for the purpose. Hyundai Electronics is planning to set up a manufacturing plant in the electronic automotive component sector near Madras. The South Korean major is said to have been keen on setting up the project on its own as it had reservations about certain clauses in the proposed pact with Elcot.
248 PROPOSALS FOR INDIAN INVESTMENT ABROAD CLEARED

The government has approved 248 proposals amounting to $215.2 million for Indian investment overseas in the current calendar year up to November 30, 1996. The quantum of proposals cleared for overseas investment has declined in the last three years. In 1994, a total of 222 proposals amounting to $336.3 million were approved and in 1995, 216 proposals amounting to $277.18 million were approved. This was disclosed by Finance Minister P. Chidambaram in the lower house of Parliament.
Business Standard
RUPEE FALLS AGAINST DOLLAR

The rupee fell by 13 paise to 35.92 per dollar on hectic buying by the State Bank of India (SBI). The SBI was in the market buying the greenback for oil companies. Some foreign exchange dealers were expecting the rupee to touch 36 per dollar as the long-overdue demand for the U.S. currency was hitting the market. The rupee rallied later in the day close at 35.88/35.90 per dollar.
$5 BLN WORLD BANK FUNDS FOR STATE ROAD PROJECTS

The decks have been cleared for a World Bank-led $5 billion investment in projects sponsored by state governments to upgrade and rehabilitate high-density road sections. The World Bank had approved the States' Road Infrastructure Development Technical Assistance loan last week. The proceeds of the loan would support the efforts of state governments in road infrastructure investment preparations. Sources said 10 states had expressed their willingness to participate in the scheme.
INDIA RAISES TELECOMMUNICATION OFFER

India agreed to improve its offer on basic telecommunication services at a meeting called by the United States to discuss the issue at the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) ministerial meeting. India's commerce secretary said the cabinet stand on this had been finalised. He added the concerned ministries had favoured the binding offer on market access for foreigners under Indian law to be raised from 25 percent to 49 percent. India now allows 49 percent foreign equity in telecommunication services companies competing with the department of telecommunications.
Financial Express
ENGINEERING MAJOR EYEING CAPTIVE POWER PROJECTS

Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL) has turned bullish on power generation. BHEL has decided to bid for captive power projects for public sector firms (PSUs) like Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Gas Authority of India (GAIL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL). BHEL has submitted technical bids for the 20 megawatt captive power plant for IOC in Mathura, Uttar Pradesh, and GAIL's 30 megawatt plant at Ganghar in Gujarat. BHEL is bidding for a 20 megawatt HPCL power project at Vizag in Andhra Pradesh. It plans to compete for HPCL's 20 megawatt plant at Bombay as well. It will also bid for the 60 to 75 megawatt captive power unit of NOCIL.
ADVANCE LICENCE SCHEME RUN INTO ROUGH WEATHER

The advance licence scheme in the 1992-97 export-import policy has run into rough weather with exporters surrendering five billion rupees worth of licences to the commerce ministry. Another popular scheme among exporters, the passbook scheme, was yet to take off. In addition to this, availability of credit remained restricted owing to high interest rates under both the pre-shipment and post-shipment schemes. These problems came on top of the minimum alternate tax provision plus the two percent across the board customs duty on all items imposed in the 1996/97 (April-March) budget. The Observer
MOTOROLA TO EXPAND INDIAN-OPERATIONS

The computer arm of the telecommunications giant Motorola Inc, Motorola Computer Group (MCG), plans to expand its operations in India. The company intends to set up new sales office in India and appoint a new country manager to develop and market a range of industry standard computers, network servers and symmetrical multiprocessor business systems. Stating this, MCG's regional manager for South-Asia Joe Khoo said the move was aimed to tap the power PC market that could grow at a rate of 50 percent in India and South Asia.
